> In two short paragraphs, say what a README is for. No tools.

▸ Thought for 2s

  A README is a text file (typically written in Markdown) that serves as the front door to a project. It gives anyone
  who encounters the repository a quick overview of what the project does, why it exists, and who it's for — making
  it the first thing a visitor reads on platforms like GitHub.

  Beyond the overview, a README usually provides practical guidance: how to install dependencies, configure the
  environment, run the code, and contribute. It reduces friction for new users and collaborators by answering the
  most common questions upfront, turning an unfamiliar codebase into something approachable.
